page: Amazon Web Services r8g.8xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by custom AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors. Operating on the arm64 architecture, it features 32 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core running at 2.8 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates on the Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight the server's memory subsystem, with read-only large block memory bandwidth reaching 402.49 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 183.47 GB/sec, both placing in the top tier. Passmark memory and database operations benchmarks also rank in the top tier, with database operations scoring 47,337.28. Multi-core performance is strong, as evidenced by a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 21,614.0. However, single-core CPU performance and LLM inference speeds represent a relative tradeoff, with single-core Geekbench and stress-ng scores falling in the average range, and large model LLM prompt processing showing weaker performance at 5.9 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r8g.8xlarge offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of hyperthreading or unused local storage. The combination of high memory bandwidth and dedicated arm64 cores makes this server type highly suitable for in-memory databases like Redis, which achieved 66.65 million operations per second in testing. It is also well-suited for large-scale database operations, static web serving, and software compilation tasks, while being less optimal for heavy single-threaded compute or large-scale LLM text generation.
